newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African central bank signs $1.75 billion loan.
newsitem.headline: S.African central bank signs $1.75 billion loan.

text.p: South Africa's central Reserve Bank said on Wednesday it had signed a syndicated medium term revolving credit facility for $1.75 billion.

It had originally aimed for $1.5 billion but the transaction was over-subscribed with the arrangers, co-arrangers and lead managers prepared to commit almost $2 billion. The Bank decided to scale down the amount to $1.75 billion.

The Bank announced in June it had completed the first phase of talks in establishing the loan, which officials said would inspire more confidence in South Africa's ability to provide liquidity when and if needed by the foreign exchange market.

The loan was arranged by 12 banks -- Bank Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Chase Manhattan, Commerzbank, CS First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Dresdner Bank, Midland Bank, J.P. Morgan, Natwest Capital Markets, Societe Generale, SBC Warburg and Union Bank of Switzerland.
In addition there were a nine co-arrangers and 13 lead managers.
